newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-ZIMBABWE SAY GROBBELAAR TO PLAY FOR THEM ON SUNDAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZIMBABWE SAY GROBBELAAR TO PLAY FOR THEM ON SUNDAY.

text.p: Zimbabwe are expecting goalkeeper Bruce Grobbelaar, who is on trial in England on charges of match-fixing, to play for them in an international on Sunday, officials said on Wednesday.

Zimbabwe Football Association secretary-general Phil Hwata said he had obtained permission from the judge in the trial in Winchester for Grobbelaar to fly to Zimbabwe for a vital African Nations Cup qualifying tie against Ghana in Harare on Sunday.
"I contacted the judge and he said it was okay for Bruce to come," Hwata told Reuters.
"He will be leaving London on Thursday night and we expect him the next morning. We are very pleased he will be able to play," he added.
Grobbelaar, 39, played for Zimbabwe earlier this month in Harare in a World Cup qualifying match against Togo, earning his 42nd cap for the country.
The goalkeeper, who plays for English second division club Plymouth Argyle, regularly travelled to Zimbabwe while on bail pending the trial.

The prosecution in the trial of Grobbelaar and three other men, which started last week, says the former Liverpool goalkeeper tried to fix at least four soccer matches in return for payments from a Far Eastern betting syndicate. Grobbelaar denies the charges.
